title: GeoPano: Towards Geometrically Accurate Panoramic 3D Reconstruction from a Single Panorama
claim: One model turns a single in-the-wild input into high-fidelity 3D geometry, and it holds up across indoor and outdoor scenes.
layout: 2x3 grid of panels, indoor left and outdoor right, orange zoom-in insets
description: A gallery of six rounded panels in a 2x3 grid. The left column is labeled Indoor and the right column Outdoor, with the labels in large orange text on a pale green tag. Each panel shows an input panorama at top left and a rainbow-colored ERP depth map beneath it. At right is a large oblique-view 3D point cloud of the scene. Orange boxes mark regions of the point cloud, and dashed orange lines link each box to a zoomed inset showing fine detail. The first panel has curved red arrows labeled Reconstruct and Re-Project that link the panorama, the point cloud and the depth map. Cyan arrows mark the viewpoint used for the zoom-in, and a legend at the bottom right explains them. The eye goes first to the colorful point clouds and the insets.
caption: For each scene, our GeoPano takes a single panorama as input, directly recovers distortion-free 3D point clouds, which can be easily re-projected into the sphere plane to obtain the ERP depth map. Given diverse in-the-wild panoramas from both indoor and outdoor scenes, GeoPano can robustly reconstruct high-fidelity 3D geometry, showing its impressive zero-shot capabilities.
abstract: Panoramic 3D reconstruction enables the holistic recovery of complete 360 $^\circ$ scene geometry, offering significant benefits for robotics and AR/VR applications. However, directly estimating geometry from ERP images is inherently challenged by spherical distortions. To reduce spherical projection distortions, a common strategy is to decompose panoramas into distortion-free perspective views, but independently processing these views often introduces cross-view geometric inconsistencies. To address these challenges, we introduce GeoPano, a feed-forward framework for single-view panoramic 3D reconstruction that recovers a geometrically accurate and consistent point cloud from a single panorama. Our approach is driven by two key innovations: First, we propose a panoramic-aware attention aggregator, featuring a streamlined attention architecture equipped with a novel Pano-Attention mechanism, which explicitly exploits the intrinsic spherical geometry of the panorama to guide cross-view interactions, thereby suppressing geometric inconsistencies. Furthermore, we formulate a hybrid supervision strategy to jointly enforce fine-grained local details in perspective space and global structural coherence in spherical space. Experiments demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms previous SOTA approaches in reconstruction accuracy, geometric consistency, and visual fidelity.
